Date: 2028-04-15T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: SvcEdge capacity plan & pilot ask

Hi Jon — great demo earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap and follow-ups so we can recommend a clear path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private):

Notes from call:
- Primary workload: real-time personalization scoring + short-form generation for recommendations.
- Target concurrency: expected steady-state ~150 QPS during business hours, with short spikes up to ~400 QPS for ~5–10 minutes every hour.
- 99th-pct latency target: ~120ms token latency end-to-end (app->model->response).
- Data residency: US-only for now; SOC 2 compliance required.

As next steps, can you confirm (a) expected daily traffic curve (peaks vs baseline), (b) whether 99th-pct 120ms is a hard requirement or a target for gradual improvement, and (c) procurement contact for pilot paperwork?

Initial guidance we discussed on the call: for steady high QPS with tight 99th latency, Dedicated reserved capacity typically gives the most predictable SLOs — we can couple that with a Hosted fallback for burst absorb. Private VPC makes sense later if you need network isolation / on-prem access, but it adds provisioning lead time.

If you confirm the traffic profile I'll loop in pricing and infra owners with a recommended sizing and a 3-month pilot proposal.

Thanks — Sergio

Sergio — thanks, this is helpful. Answers below inline.

Traffic curve (typical day):
- Baseline: ~100–160 QPS between 7am–7pm PT.
- Recurring micro-bursts: every ~45–60 minutes we see a ~5–10 minute spike reaching ~350–420 QPS from localized events (campaign pushes).
- Night/weekend: drops below 20 QPS.

Latency: 99th-pct 120ms is our goal for the user-facing path. We can tolerate a soft period during pilot but we'd like to measure to that bar.

Compliance: SOC 2 is required. Data is US-only for now.

Procurement: Elena Torres (elena@svcedge.com) handles procurement/contracting. Please copy Elena for paperwork.

Question: Given our spikes, can Hosted alone handle this reliably without an enormous cost? If not, what lead time and cost delta to get Dedicated or Private?

—Jon

Subject: Re: SvcEdge capacity plan & pilot ask — proposed pilot + sizing (attachments)

Thanks for the context — copied Jon for transparency. Attaching a short mutual action plan and a sample throughput CSV from a similar retail workload for reference. (attachments: SvcEdge_MutualActionPlan.pdf, svcedge-throughput-sample.csv)

High-level proposal (pilot):
- Duration: 3 months.
- Recommended pattern: Reserve Dedicated pool sized for baseline throughput + autoscale/burst to Hosted for short spikes. This gives predictable 99th latency while avoiding heavy overprovisioning for transient events.

Sizing (ballpark):
- Baseline target: 150 QPS steady. Recommend reserving capacity equivalent to 6–8 A100-eq GPUs (model-dependent) to comfortably sustain baseline and keep KV cache warm.
- Burst headroom: allow routing to 2–4 Hosted instances (autoscale) to absorb 350–420 QPS spikes without increasing tail latency. We can implement burst routing with weighted policy and a warm standby pool.
- SLA & runbook: we can commit to 99.9% availability for Dedicated pool for pilot; tail latency SLOs to be measured and reported daily.

Private VPC note: onboarding Private/VPC adds 6–8 weeks lead time and a one-time set-up fee; we'll scope separately if SvcEdge needs full isolation. Private would be recommended if contractual constraints require customer-managed network or stricter control over keys.

Next asks for Jon/Elena:
1) Confirm procurement contact (Elena) — can you share email and preferred DocuSign contact?
2) Any blackout windows or expected maintenance windows we should avoid during the pilot?
3) Confirm whether you want us to price the pilot as "Dedicated-only" or "Dedicated+Hosted fallback" (we recommend the latter).

I'll draft a one-page BOM and a DocuSign-ready pilot MSA for signatures once we have the procurement contact.

—Monica

Monica / Sergio — this looks good. We are interested in the Dedicated+Hosted fallback approach. Confirming procurement contact: Elena Torres (elena@svcedge.com) — copied here.

A couple quick items before we sign:
- Please provide a one-page BOM with estimated monthly run-rate for the pilot (include both Dedicated reserve and expected Hosted burst costs).
- We will need IP allowlisting, a short Data Retention clause (30 days log retention for pilot) and SOC 2 attestation in the pilot MSA. Can you confirm those can be included?
- For Private VPC: we want to evaluate it in parallel; if Dedicated pilot goes well, we'll start Private onboarding immediately (we understand the 6–8 week lead time).

Also, can Hosted be used as the temporary path while Private is being provisioned? We expect some legal review, so that would help speed time-to-value.

If you can drop the BOM and a DocuSign link by EOD tomorrow we'll route to Elena and legal on our side.

—Jon
